ORDINANCE XXIV OF 1997
ORDINANCE XXIV OF 1997
OFFENCES IN RESPECT OF BANKS
(SPECIAL COURTS) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance further to amend the
Offences in Respect of Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1984
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary,
Part I, 4th February, 1997]
No. F.2(1)/97‑Pub., dated 4‑2‑1997.‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:‑
Whereas it is expedient further to
amend the Offences in Respect of Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1984 (IX of
1984) for the purpose hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied, that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan the President s pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
1. Short title and commencement.‑‑(1) This Ordinance may
be called the Offences in Respect of Banks (Special Courts) (Amendment)
Ordinance, 1997.
(2) It shall come into force at once

information:‑
Whereas it is expedient further to
amend the Offences in Respect of Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1984 (IX of
1984) for the purpose hereinafter appearing;
And whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied, that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now, therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan the President s pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
2. Amendment of section 3, Ordinance
IX of 1984.‑‑In
the Offences in Respect of Banks (Special Courts) Ordinance, 1984 (IX of 1984),
in section 3, after subsection (1) the following new subsections shall be
added, namely:‑‑
"(1A) A person to be appointed
as Special Court under subsection (1) shall be appointed in consultation with
the High Court in which the Special Court is established and shall hold office
for a term of three years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
(1B) a person, not being a Judge of
a High Court, appointed as Special Court under this section may, by notice in
writing under his hand addressed to the Federal Government resign from his
office, or may be removed from his office on the ground of misconduct".
